capitals.name: Skopje
capitals.note: The text says the capital was 'in Skopje'; the infobox lists Prizren, Skopje and Serres. Dušan died at his court in Prizren (Stefan Dušan page); Serres was Dušan's base in 1345 and later the seat of Helena and Jovan Uglješa's autonomous principality (Stefan Uroš V page). The Uroš V page is silent on his capital.

rulers.name: Stefan Dušan
rulers.title: Emperor and autocrat of Serbs and Romans
rulers.note: Crowned 16 April 1346 at Skopje; died 20 December 1355 (he had ruled Serbia as king since before 1346).

rulers.name: Stefan Uroš V
rulers.title: Emperor
rulers.note: King (co-ruler) 1346-1355, Emperor 1355-1371; died childless 2 or 4 December 1371. Vukašin Mrnjavčević was co-ruler with the title of king 1365-1371 (Serbian Empire page).

correction.text: the Kingdom of Serbia plus the Byzantine lands taken by 1345 (Macedonia to Kavala, Serres, without Thessaloniki)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1346, which Cliopatria draws as its Kingdom of Serbia row (to 1351). Dušan's offensive 'began in 1342' and took Byzantine lands 'as far as Kavala' but 'not the Peloponnesus or Thessaloniki'; Serres fell on 25 September 1345 and he was crowned Emperor at Skopje on 16 April 1346. The kingdom shape plus the Macedonian conquests is the researcher's reading; the page gives no map. The Karl Thopia page (opened for the date of the Serbian conquest of Albania, title 'King of Serbia, Albania and the coast' in 1343) is silent on it: it shows only that Durrës was still Angevin in 1350, so the date stays undated.

correction.text: the empire after 1347: the 1352 shape without Thessaly, which falls in 1348

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1347. 'In 1347, Dušan conquered Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania' and made his half-brother Simeon Uroš governor. Cliopatria's 1352 empire shape (186,880 km2, to the Gulf of Corinth) without Thessaly is the closest drawable reading.

correction.text: the full 1352 shape, valid from the conquest of Thessaly in 1348; unchanged, only the years are corrected

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1348-1351: 'In 1348, Dušan also conquered Thessaly, appointing Preljub as governor'. Cliopatria's first empire shape (1352) already holds the whole, so its extent is extended back to 1348 (years only).

186,880 km2, 'circa 1355' (caption of the maximum extent, 'from the Danube in the north to the Gulf of Corinth in the south'); the page and the Dušan page give no km2 figure, so the area cannot be compared with the infobox. The shape is right only to Dušan's death (20 December 1355); the pages show the empire 'fragmented into a conglomeration of principalities' from 1356. Years 1356-1362 pass to the new keyframe serbian-empire_1356. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1352..1355 from this entry's own 'valid 1352-1355 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: the 1352 shape without Thessaly, Epirus, Aetolia-Acarnania (Dytiki Ellada), Kostur (Kastoria) and the Valona counties (independent after 1355); the rest of Albania, in the hands of autonomous lords (the Balšić of Zeta and Shkodër named in Uroš's edicts), stays inside as nominal land until Maritsa in 1371, and so do the autonomous lords' lands in Macedonia and the west

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1356-1371. Spring 1356: Nikephoros Orsini 'landed a force on the coast of Thessaly and quickly overran it', drove Simeon Uroš 'from Aetolia and Acarnania', and Simeon, 'retreating to Epirus and western Macedonia, seized Kostur and proclaimed himself Tsar' (Kostur is drawn out of the shape; Epirus went to Orsini, who 're-established himself in Epirus in 1356, to which he also added Thessaly' on the Despotate of Epirus page); in 1359 Simeon retook Epirus and Thessaly and ruled them as 'emperor of Serbs and Greeks'. Valona, a vassal 1346-1355, was independent after Dušan's death (Valona page), so its three counties leave the shape. Albania stays: the Battle of Maritsa page has 'Thessaly, Albania and Epirus had entirely seceded from Serbia' by 1371 but no page opened dates the secession (Stefan Uroš V, Karl Thopia, Balšić and Despotate of Epirus pages are silent; Durrës was Angevin until 1367/68 and the Balšić were still 'oblastni gospodari of Zeta' in Uroš's edicts), so Albania leaves the shape only in the ledger's 1371 loss. Helena and Jovan Uglješa ruled 'autonomously from the Principality of Serres'; the Dejanović, Balšić and Altomanović were 'similarly autonomous' (the page gives no lands), so the remaining shape is soft.

correction.text: not used: replaced by serbian-empire_1356 for 1363-1371; the years 1372-1374 belong to the successor states

keyframe_review.note: 184,871 km2, held to 1374 by Cliopatria. Not usable: for 1363-1371 the shape of serbian-empire_1356 applies; the empire 'effectively ended with the death of Uroš V in 1371' (Serbian Empire page) after Maritsa (26 September 1371), and 1372-1374 belong to the successor principalities (Moravian Serbia, the Ottoman vassals in Macedonia, Zeta, Albania, Epirus). region.text: the modern counties of Vlorë (Valona), Fier and Berat ('Area: the modern counties of Vlore (Valona), Fier, and Berat')

ledger.note: 1346: Valona becomes a Serbian vassal principality. 'Valona fell in late 1345 or early 1346' and Dušan placed his brother-in-law John Komnenos Asen in charge, with Kanina and Berat as the main fortresses; infobox 'vassal of the Serbian Empire (1346–1355)'. Some scholars date the taking of Valona and Kanina to 1337. Region corrected by the repair of 2026-10-25: the earlier region, Cliopatria's 'Principality of Valona and Kanina' 1395 shape, lies east of Vlorë and Kanina (bbox 19.70-21.21 E; Vlorë is at 19.49 E), so it leaves out the capital; the page names the three counties.

region.text: the Serbian lands and the Macedonian conquests of 1342-1345 (the page names Serres, Ohrid, Prilep, Strumica and 'lands as far as Kavala')

ledger.note: 16 April 1346: Dušan is crowned Emperor at Skopje. 'On 16 April 1346, in Skopje, he had himself crowned'; Patriarch Joanikije II crowned him 'Emperor and autocrat of Serbs and Romans' after a council at Serres had proclaimed him 'Tsar of the Serbs and Romans' around Christmas 1345 (Stefan Dušan page).

union.text: Aetolia and Acarnania, up to the Gulf of Corinth

ledger.note: 1347: Dušan takes Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania. 'In 1347, Dušan conquered Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania' and put Simeon Uroš in charge.

1348: Dušan takes Thessaly. 'In 1348, Dušan also conquered Thessaly, appointing Preljub as governor.' The Catalan Duchy of Neopatras held southern Thessaly (next event); this event is the Byzantine part.

region.text: 'most of the Duchy's possessions in Thessaly'; Neopatras itself stayed Catalan

ledger.note: 1348: the Catalan part of Thessaly goes to the Serbs. 'Most of the Duchy's possessions in Thessaly were lost when the region was conquered by the Serbs of Stefan Dushan in 1348'; 'Neopatras and the region around it remained in Catalan hands'. The region is the one the catalan-company dossier records as its 1348 loss to serbian-empire; the page does not say whether Zetounion (Lamia) survived.

region.text: part of northern Serbia (district names the researcher's)

ledger.note: 1354: Hungary invades northern Serbia. 'In 1354, Dušan was attacked by the Hungarians who managed to occupy part of northern Serbia.' The page names no district; Mačva, Belgrade and Braničevo are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the modern counties of Vlorë (Valona), Fier and Berat ('Area: the modern counties of Vlore (Valona), Fier, and Berat')

ledger.note: 1355: Valona becomes independent. 'After Dušan died in 1355, John became an independent lord, though he stayed under strong Venetian influence' (infobox: 'independent (1355–1417)'). Region corrected by the repair of 2026-10-25: the earlier region, Cliopatria's 'Principality of Valona and Kanina' 1395 shape, lies east of Vlorë and Kanina (bbox 19.70-21.21 E; Vlorë is at 19.49 E), so it leaves out the capital; the page names the three counties.
May 1355: peace with Hungary. 'Peace with Louis I of Hungary was concluded in May 1355.' Dušan died on 20 December 1355 while preparing a crusade against the Turks.

union.text: Aetolia and Acarnania, up to the Gulf of Corinth

ledger.note: Spring 1356: Orsini takes Thessaly from the Serbs. 'In the spring of 1356, Nikephoros Orsini landed a force on the coast of Thessaly and quickly overran it', driving Simeon Uroš 'from Aetolia and Acarnania'. Counterpart set to despotate-of-epirus by the eu-18-d reviewer: Nikephoros II Orsini restored the Despotate of Epirus in 1356 (that dossier records the gain from serbian-empire in 1356). Epirus added by the repair of 2026-10-25: the Despotate of Epirus page has Nikephoros II 'reestablish himself in Epirus in 1356, to which he also added Thessaly' (and 'killed in battle putting down an Albanian revolt in 1359', when Simeon took the lands over); Simeon's seat in 1356 is Kostur, not Epirus (next event).

region.text: Kostur (Kastoria), seized by Simeon Uroš in 1356

ledger.counterpart: Simeon Uroš (Emperor of Serbs and Greeks)
ledger.note: 1356: Simeon Uroš breaks away at Kostur (Kastoria). Driven from Aetolia and Acarnania by Orsini, he 'retreating to Epirus and western Macedonia, seized Kostur and proclaimed himself Tsar'; the Sabor held in Skopje 'did not accept Simeon's claims'. The page gives no separate year for Kostur (it is in the 1356 context). In 1358 he failed against Zeta and in 1359 retook Epirus and Thessaly as 'emperor of Serbs and Greeks'. Region corrected by the repair of 2026-10-25: the earlier region, Epirus, went to Orsini in 1356 (previous event).

minus.text: the modern counties of Vlorë (Valona), Fier and Berat ('Area: the modern counties of Vlore (Valona), Fier, and Berat')

region.text: Albania outside the Valona counties: the lands of the Balšić of Shkodër, the Thopia of Krujë and the other lords that 'had entirely seceded' by 1371

ledger.note: By 1371: the Battle of Maritsa page has 'Thessaly, Albania and Epirus had entirely seceded from Serbia' by 1371; no page opened dates the secession (the Balšić page: the brothers were 'oblastni gospodari of Zeta' in edicts of Uroš (r. 1355-1371) and set up 'their own independent state' after Maritsa and the collapse of central authority, no year; the Karl Thopia page: Durrës Angevin until 1367/68, Karl lord of Krujë from 1358, no Serbian rule mentioned). The loss is therefore entered at the end of the empire's life, as a bridge (confidence 1), and Albania stays in the 1356-1371 keyframe. The Valona counties left in 1355 (vassal_end).

region.text: Macedonia, from Serres to the Vardar, and parts of central Serbia

ledger.note: 26 September 1371: the Ottomans beat the Serbs at Maritsa. 'fought on 26 September 1371 near the Maritsa River', 'a decisive Ottoman victory in which both Serbian commanders were killed'; 'Ottoman troops advanced into Macedonia and parts of central Serbia', 'the decline of Serbian power in Macedonia'.

December 1371: the empire ends and the Macedonian lords fall into the Ottoman orbit (the page says regional lords like Prince Marko 'became Ottoman vassals'); the end of the contest at the dissolution is the researcher's bridge, since the page does not say when the Ottoman advance stopped. The Prince Marko page (opened to date the end) has Marko 'the formal sovereign of Serbia' on 2 or 4 December 1371, an Ottoman vassal only 'sometime after 1371' and 'probably not immediately after the Battle of Maritsa', and is silent on when the advance stopped, so the end stays a bridge.

ledger.note: 4 December 1371: Uroš V dies childless and the empire ends. 'Stefan Uroš V died childless on 4 December 1371' (Uroš V page: '2/4 December'); 'The Serbian Empire effectively ended with the death of Uroš V in 1371'; 'the Empire continued to be ruled by semi-independent provincial lords'. Lazar Hrebeljanović's principality on the Morava is established the same year.

wars.name: Serbian conquest of Byzantine lands

union.text: most of Macedonia as far as Kavala, without Thessaloniki
Aetolia and Acarnania, up to the Gulf of Corinth

zones.text: Macedonia to Kavala, Epirus, Aetolia, Acarnania, Thessaly

wars.outcome: Serbian victory: Serres (25 September 1345), the Athonite monks (November 1345), Epirus, Aetolia and Acarnania (1347) and Thessaly (1348); Dušan took no Peloponnese and no Thessaloniki.
wars.note: The page dates the offensive from 1342 and uses the Byzantine civil war; before 1346 the state was the Kingdom of Serbia (peace of 26 August 1334 gave Ohrid, Prilep and Strumica). The Duchy of Neopatras page adds the Catalan part of Thessaly (1348), whose Duchy kept Neopatras.

wars.name: Dušan's war in Bosnia and Hum
wars.outcome: Dušan 'invaded Hum' in October 1350 with an army 'said to be of 80,000'; Ban Stephen II Kotromanić avoided battle and the page records no final result.
wars.note: No border change is dated, so no zone is recorded.

wars.name: Hungarian invasion of Serbia
wars.outcome: The Hungarians 'managed to occupy part of northern Serbia' in 1354; peace with Louis I in May 1355.

wars.name: Orsini's invasion of Thessaly

union.text: Aetolia and Acarnania, up to the Gulf of Corinth
Kostur (Kastoria), seized by Simeon Uroš in 1356

wars.outcome: Orsini overran Thessaly in spring 1356 and drove Simeon Uroš from Aetolia and Acarnania; Simeon retook Epirus and Thessaly in 1359 under his own 'emperor of Serbs and Greeks' title. Simeon seized Kostur and proclaimed himself Tsar in 1356; Orsini re-established himself in Epirus in 1356 (Despotate of Epirus page).

wars.name: Battle of Maritsa
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory on 26 September 1371; Vukašin and Uglješa Mrnjavčević killed; Ottoman troops advanced into Macedonia and Prince Marko and other lords became Ottoman vassals; Uroš V died in December and the empire ended.

certainty.note: No treaty line survives in the pages opened for the empire's frontiers; the 1334 peace with Byzantium (Ohrid, Prilep, Strumica) pre-dates it, and the Danube-Sava northern border is the one firm line (Stefan Lazarević page for the later period). After 1355 the shape is soft because autonomous lords held much of it.

sources.title: Karl Thopia

sources.title: Balsic noble family
sources.note: The Balsic brothers acknowledged as 'oblastni gospodari of Zeta' in edicts of Emperor Uros (r. 1355-1371), seat Shkoder; their own independent state after Maritsa (no year).

sources.title: Prince Marko
sources.note: Marko formal sovereign of Serbia on 2 or 4 December 1371; an Ottoman vassal 'sometime after 1371', probably not immediately after Maritsa; silent on the end of the Ottoman advance.

notes: Cliopatria's Serbian Empire row (1352..1458) is two or three states: the Empire proper (1346-1371), Lazar's Moravian Serbia (1371-1402) and the Serbian Despotate (1402-1459, per the Despotate page; the Moravian Serbia page says the state 'became known as the Serbian Despotate in 1402'). This dossier keeps the Empire (shapes 1352 and 1363, plus new keyframes 1346-1351 and 1356-1371) and marks the eight later shapes wrong for it; the new dossier moravian-serbia reviews them. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Serbia row covers 1346-1351 and must end in 1346 in the kingdom-of-serbia dossier to avoid double drawing. Infobox area: the Serbian Empire page and the Dušan page give no km2 figure (Cliopatria 186,880 km2 for 1352), so the area check is not possible; the extent is only 'from the Danube in the north to the Gulf of Corinth in the south'. Not on the pages opened: the Serres principality of Helena and Uglješa after 1371, the Dejanović, Balšić and Altomanović lands (the pages call them 'autonomous' only), Albania south of the Mat (the title 'King of Serbia, Albania and the coast' is of 1343 and the page gives no conquest year), Dušan's wars against Bulgaria after 1330 and the 1334 peace's land beyond Ohrid, Prilep and Strumica (pre-dates the empire). Names for the gazetteer: none new; Aetolia and Acarnania are drawn by a 70 km radius at 21.3 E, 38.65 N because the gazetteer lacks the region. The successors' counterpart strings 'Nikephoros II Orsini' and 'Simeon Uroš (Emperor of Serbs and Greeks)' are persons, not states; a gap-filler may map them to despotate-of-epirus / despotate-of-arta (eu-05). Repairs of 2026-10-25 (review eu-18-d): the 1356-1371 keyframe keeps Albania (minus the Valona counties, independent in 1355) until a 1371 loss to albanian-principalities, because no page dates the secession (Stefan Uroš V, Karl Thopia, Balšić and Despotate of Epirus pages opened: silent; the Maritsa page's 'by 1371' is the only bound); Simeon's 1356 seat is Kostur (Kastoria, not in the gazetteer: drawn by a 30 km radius at 21.27 E, 40.52 N) and Epirus is Orsini's; the Valona vassal region is now the three counties; the Catalan part of Thessaly is a second 1348 gain. Disagreement: the Despotate of Epirus page dates Dušan's conquest of Epirus to 1348, the Stefan Dušan page to 1347 (the Dušan page is followed). Name needed by the gazetteer: Kastoria (place/admin1, Greece, 40.52 N, 21.27 E).
